point of the other with respect to $A$, or if $C$ is the centre and $B$
the inverse point of the first sphere, $C^{\prime}$ will be the inverse point,
and $B^{\prime}$ the centre of the second.
Now let a quantity $e^{\prime}$ of electricity be communicated to the
second sphere, and let it be uninfluenced by external forces. It
will become uniformly distributed over the sphere with a surface-
density
$$\sigma^{\prime}=\frac{e^{\prime}}{4 \pi l^{\prime 2}} .$$
(21)
Its action at any point outside the sphere will be the same as
that of a charge $e^{\prime}$ placed at $B^{\prime}$ the centre of the sphere.
At the spherical surface and within it the potential is
$$P^{\prime}=\frac{e^{\prime}}{a^{\prime}},$$
(22)
a constant quantity.
Now let us invert this system. The centre $B^{\prime}$ becomes in the
inverted system the inverse point $B$, and the charge $e^{\prime}$ at $B^{\prime}$
becomes $e^{\prime} \frac{R}{f^{\prime}}$ at $B$, and at any point separated from $B$ by the
surface the potential is that due to this charge at $B$.
The potential at any point $P$ on the spherical surface, or on
the same side as $B$, is in the inverted system
$$\frac{e^{\prime}}{a^{\prime}} \frac{R}{A P} .$$
If we now superpose on this system a charge $e$ at $A$, where
$$e=-\frac{e^{\prime}}{a^{\prime}} R$$
(23)
the potential on the spherical surface, and at all points on the
same side as $B$, will be reduced to zero. At all points on the
same side as $A$ the potential will be that due to a charge $e$ at $A$,
and a charge $e^{\prime} \frac{R}{f^{\prime}}$ at $B$.
But
$$e^{\prime} \frac{R}{f^{\prime}}=-e \frac{a^{\prime}}{f^{\prime}}=-e \frac{a}{f^{\prime}},$$
(24)
as we found before for the charge of the image at $B$.
To find the density at any point of the first sphere we have
$$\sigma=\sigma^{\prime} \frac{R^{3}}{A P^{3}} .$$
(25)
Substituting for the value of $\sigma^{\prime}$ in terms of the quantities be-
longing to the first sphere, we find the same value as in Art 158,
$$\sigma=-\frac{e\left(f^{2}-a^{2}\right)}{4 \pi a A P^{3}} .$$
(26)
